# Locked consumer for the Node 22.12 package floor

This fixture installs the tarball built by `readme-smoke` in the same workflow run. It uses a committed npm v3 consumer lock and `npm ci --ignore-scripts --engine-strict`; it does not resolve a new dependency graph in CI. Registry versions and SHA-512 integrity values are reviewed here. Fixture-only overrides select the runtime versions already pinned by the repository lock; they do not alter the published package or its pnpm overrides.

`SAME_RUN_TARBALL_SHA512` is an explicit template marker, not a usable digest. The preparation script checks the packed package's version, dependency classes, platform/engine constraints and bin targets against the lock, then replaces only that marker with the local same-run tarball's SHA-512. Registry entries remain unchanged. The producer also captures exact installed runtime versions and registry URLs using `pnpm list --prod --depth Infinity --json` after its frozen install. The sanitized `runtime-dependencies.json` is uploaded with the tarball and includes its SHA-512. Preparation compares every pinned consumer entry against that same-run manifest before changing the lock, so a resolved Zod4.6.8 with an unchanged ^4.6.7 spec cannot silently test Zod4.6.7. npm normalizes leading `./` on bin paths; the preparation comparison accounts for that representation difference. Missing or stale fixture metadata fails before installation.

The package's own version is the one value that follows a release automatically. The release workflow's version step (`pnpm version-packages`: `changeset version`, then `scripts/sync-floor-fixture-version.mjs`) sets only the `version` of the `node_modules/market-data-sanity-checker` entry to the bumped `package.json` version, so the bump and the fixture change land in the same reviewed Version Packages commit. The sync script refuses, leaving the lock untouched, when anything else would have to change: dependency ranges, bin targets, engines or platform constraints that differ from `package.json`, a changed `resolved` or integrity marker, or a lock not in npm's formatting.

When resolved runtime versions change in the repository lock (even with identical manifest specs), or runtime metadata, engines or bin targets change, update this fixture deliberately: stage a tarball from the reviewed source at `market-data-sanity-checker.tgz`, update fixture-only pins to the reviewed repository runtime versions, and generate a new consumer lock with npm10.9 on Node22.12 using `npm install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund --engine-strict` in a temporary consumer directory. Replace only the own-package integrity with `SAME_RUN_TARBALL_SHA512`, review the complete dependency diff and validate `npm ci` plus the existing CLI assertions before copying the lock back. Never generate or refresh the registry lock during the floor job.

This checks one reproducible consumer graph. It does not test every future version allowed by runtime semver ranges, prove registry ownership, or attest the source of the build. The local tarball is intentionally variable across source changes; the upload/download pair continues to select the artifact of this workflow run. No scripts from installed dependencies are run. No scanners are suppressed; final public CI and scanner evidence must be reviewed before claiming findings resolved.

The current runtime graph consists of three direct registry packages without transitive dependencies. Capture deliberately rejects runtime aliases, optional roots and new transitive/optional child dependencies until their fixture support is explicitly reviewed. It does not silently flatten or partially validate a larger graph. The manifest is bound to the local tarball digest, package name and version; a missing, mismatched or stale manifest fails before npm ci. This is build-job evidence, not an independently signed attestation.
